transcript: you probably know the beloved Tony and Emmy-winning actor Sean Hayes who's currently performing in this psychological thriller off broadway but if you don't know the playwright David Cale you're missing out because he has really mastered the art of this format: the narrative solo play. The Unknown is about a writer who realizes he has a staIker and he begins this sort of battle of wits to try to get the upper hand on his staIker and even beyond that there's a bunch of twists and turns that really keep you on the edge of your seat in a way that few playwrights are able to do period let alone with only one actor. It definitely has a pulpy vibe to it which might not be for everybody some of the stuff that happens in this play is definitely kind of far-fetched but i find that kind of thing very fun and i think they leaned into it just the right amount. then of course, there's Sean Hayes who delivers a pretty impressive performance that kind of breaks the mould from the work he's usually known for. the flip side of that is i don't know that this play felt quite as tailor-made for him as some of the other solo shows we've seen on stage recently. like i couldn't escape the feeling that this role could be played very well, if not better, by plenty of other actors which isn't to say it was bad by any means in fact i actually thought it was quite good it just wasn't that striking marriage of actor and role that i think might have elevated the material even more. still though, if you're a big fan of Sean Hayes, or even if you're just a fan of this sort of classic pulpy mystery thriller then the Unknown could definitely be worth checking out before it closes on April 12th
